![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14233096/assets/0a380bff517befb89bd26c88aeb014b36b4040b5d8b5ceab6c8ef7b8549b3378.png)

Find the equation of the line that passes through the points $(2,1)$ and $(5,7).$
question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{7-1}{5-2} \\  & =\frac{6}{3} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=2$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach

$$
y=2x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2x+b \\ 1 & =2(2)+b \\ 1 & =4+b \\ 1-4 & =b \\ -3 & =b\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is $y=2x-3.$
